summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and gout was admitted after a fall at home, presenting with rigors and elevated lactate. Initial concern for infection led to broad-spectrum antibiotics, but blood and urine cultures showed no growth, and symptoms were attributed to a gout flare and anterior tibialis tendinopathy. The patient experienced vomiting, resolved with a soft diet after identifying poor dentition as the cause. A planned steroid injection for tendonitis was aborted due to a partial tear identified on ultrasound. Colchicine was restarted, allopurinol increased, and a prednisone taper initiated for gout. The patient improved clinically, remained afebrile off antibiotics, and was discharged home on a revised medication regimen with outpatient follow-up for orthopedic evaluation.
problems: Partial tear of anterior tibialis tendon
